key_gap: vs baseline: both produced the identical decision rule (fake-door first, 2 wks/$2K, ≥120/800 or ≥20% CTR vs baseline; concierge second, 3 wks/$12K, ≥40% weekly-active; $450K build gated on both; not-tested set declared) — v5's gap was ordering and ownership: the AI generated a full alternative set before the smallest probe was obvious, reached the insight only in REVIEW, and scored 3/5 efficiency vs the human's 5/5. The v6 routed run closed that gap in-pass: the m070 evidence-graded SWOT dropped the 71% survey as a strength in-frame (opinion, not behavior), the m073 strategic-interaction pass made the fake door the first countermove to the VP's commitment move, and the m019 adversary gate added a calibration the human asserted but did not ground — CTR read against the firm's baseline email-open rate, not the raw 800, so a 20% CTR is ~50% of openers. The human retained the efficiency edge (one first-pass move vs routed machinery) and ownership of the signature line; the routed AI retained the uncertainty/calibration edge.
learning_signal: On decide/maximize product signatures with stated-preference evidence, routing an evidence-graded SWOT (m070) + strategic-interaction pass (m073) with the m019 adversary gate converts 'smallest behavioral probe first' from a REVIEW repair into first-pass output, and adds threshold calibration (CTR vs baseline engagement) the pure style asserts: pre-commit bars BEFORE the email sends, grade every SWOT item by evidence strength and drop unsupported ones (a 71% stated-intent survey fails the bar), and keep the test-vs-product declaration (what the probe does NOT test + the earned second loop) as a packet line.
suggested_improvement: Keep m070+m073 dual-route on product/decide signatures (router confident=no, m084 synthesis context); make baseline-rate calibration (CTR vs baseline open/click rates on the reachable population) a standing m019 contract line whenever thresholds are set against a reachable list; keep the m090 contract — smallest experiment producing a learning signal on the core assumption + MVP-theater guard — as a mandatory packet line on assumption-gated commitments.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure style executed its core move correctly and failed on it (MVP theater) — hypothesis formed, smallest experiment run, pre-committed bar beaten (80% ≥ 40%), 'validated, commit' — but the pilot gated the LOWEST-risk assumption (clinical adoption) while the gating facts (EMR integration certification, security, HIPAA, production false-alarm rate) were never testable by any small experiment, and the reflex at the real commitment was another un-testable sandbox pilot that blows the 5-week board gate and slips go-live ~10 months. The v6 routed run held the v5 win and made the anti-theater guard mechanical: the m033 experiment-design contract proves the sandbox pilot has no control (sandbox ≠ production), no outcome measure (certification is an audit fact), and no decision-changing result; the m094 critical-reading pass names the COO's validate-first slogan as the rhetorical trap (it smuggles the premise that a small experiment CAN validate this commitment); P2 tempo mode prices the 10-month slip and commits at DO (deposit + reviews now, parallel instrumentation, staged rollout with a pre-committed false-alarm-rate stop gate as the real experiment).
learning_signal: On deadline/decide signatures with a pilot result in hand, the gating facts are often not falsifiable within the window: the smallest responsible unit is the commitment itself, and the production rollout — staged cutover with a pre-committed monitoring gate — IS the experiment. Install the anti-theater gate before approving any new pilot: (a) does it have a control, a measured outcome, and a result that could change the decision within the horizon? (b) is any gating fact an audit/lead-time commitment that no experiment can produce? if either fails, the pilot is a stall priced at the window; pair the experiment-design contract (m033) with critical-reading (m094) on validated-vendor adoption signatures, and keep tempo mode on deadline signatures so commit-at-DO beats the experiment reflex.
suggested_improvement: Install the anti-theater gate as a standing module: before any pilot is approved, require (1) control + blinding + exact outcome measure, (2) a result that can change the decision within the window, (3) a testability partition naming which gating facts no experiment can produce (those become commitment items, not evidence gaps); pair m033 with m094 on vendor-adoption signatures (rhetoric detection of 'validation' claims); keep P2 tempo mode on deadline signatures so the decision commits at DO with the experiment staged into the rollout.
